title: The indestructible tardigrade
text: Imagine an animal that can survive in space, in boiling water and in ice. It sounds impossible, but it exists. It is called the tardigrade, and it is smaller than a grain of sand.

Tardigrades are also called water bears, because they look like tiny bears with eight legs. They live almost everywhere: on mountains, in the deep ocean and even in the moss of your garden. If you look at a piece of wet moss with a microscope, you will probably find one.

Their secret is a special state called the tun. If there is no water, a tardigrade dries up and turns into a little ball. Its body almost stops working. If you add water, even many years later, it wakes up and walks away as if nothing happened.

In this state, tardigrades can survive temperatures of minus two hundred degrees and more than one hundred and fifty degrees. In 2007, scientists sent some tardigrades into space. When the tardigrades came back to Earth, many of them were still alive.
Scientists study tardigrades because they want to learn how to protect cells. If we understand their secrets, we might keep medicines safe without a fridge, or protect astronauts on long trips.

grammar.title: Grammar: the zero conditional
grammar.rule: Use the zero conditional for things that are always true: If + present simple, present simple.
rows: If there is no water, it dries up.
If you add water, it wakes up.
If you heat ice, it melts.
If it is cold, it does not move.
